title: The Nose Wall
logline: Arthur Hobbs trusts Marshall with his beloved dog Tugboat for the weekend, and Marshall loses him within six hours. While the gang searches (Robin by scent, Ted by typography, Barney by open casting call, Lily by extortion), Marshall has to keep the truth from Arthur, who turns out to be keeping a secret of his own.

guests.name: Mona Kittredge
guests.role: A professional dog walker who knows every dog on the Upper West Side by name and none of their owners: everyone is just Biscuit's mom or Tugboat's dad. Breathless, always mid-walk, oddly wise about where runaway dogs go.

continuity.era: loose; Marshall works for Arthur Hobbs

facts.marshall.job: lawyer at the firm, reporting to Arthur Hobbs
facts.arthur.dog: Tugboat: scruffy brown mutt, one ear up, 'sailor', one sausage a day
facts.arthur.lullaby: sings Tugboat to sleep: 'Little tugboat, the harbor's dark and wide'
facts.arthur.backstory: after his wife left, a month on MacLaren's stool three with puppy Tugboat
facts.arthur.tugboat_health: Tugboat's heart is enlarged; vet said 1-2 years, he lived five
facts.carl.arthur: Carl knows Arthur; Tugboat sleeps on Carl's feet behind the bar
facts.marshall.review: Arthur's review: weakness 'lost my dog', strength 'told me'
facts.barney.godson: godfather to a Pomeranian named Steve (fake dog food casting call)
facts.ted.rooftop_brick: Ted props the roof stairwell door with a brick and defends it

opens.note: Arthur and Tugboat spend most Friday nights on stool three at MacLaren's. The gang pretends not to see him.
Ted has a lunch date with the man who called his lost-dog flyer to ask about the lettering.

scenes.summary: Cold open on the outcome: Marshall alone on the roof with an empty leash. Lily arrives. The dog took the hot dog.

beats.line: Tugboat! Tugboat, buddy, come on out!
Marshmallow? Why are you holding a leash with nothing on the end of it?
Lilypad, I need you to stay very calm.
Baby, I'm calm. You're the one screaming at a water tower.
I put him down for one second to eat a hot dog. Now I don't have a dog.
Did you at least finish the hot dog?
He took it with him.

scenes.summary: Six hours earlier. Arthur Hobbs hands Marshall his dog for the weekend: rules, threats, and one unguarded goodbye in which he calls Marshall by his first name.

beats.line: Six hours earlier.
Eriksen! Here. Now.
Mr. Hobbs, if this is about the stapler, it was already sideways when I—
I have a deposition in Cleveland this weekend. Tugboat can't come.
Somebody has to keep him until Sunday. I've chosen you.
Me? Sir, that's like being handed the Olympic torch. If the torch had ears.
He eats at six. He sleeps at nine. One sausage a day.
He will lie to you about the sausage.
How does a dog lie?
He looks at you like nobody has ever fed him. Somebody has. Constantly.
And keep him out of bars. He has a history.
With what?
We don't discuss it.
You be good for Marshall, sailor. I'll be back before you know it.
Eriksen. If anything happens to him, don't come in Monday. Don't come in anywhere.
He called me Marshall.

scenes.summary: Friday night, after the roof. War council: Marshall's panic, Ted's brick, and each friend's method.

beats.line: Arthur Hobbs once fired a guy for sneezing in a deposition. Mid-sneeze.
He went into the sneeze employed and came out of it unemployed.
You lost a dog on a roof? Marshall, that's not losing a dog. That's a magic trick.
Somebody propped the stairwell door open with a brick again.
That brick has a purpose, Lily.
Okay. I'll track him.
Track him?
When I was eight, my dad sent me into the woods for three days to track a moose.
Did you find it?
I came back riding it.
I'll design a flyer.
Of course you will.
Not a flyer. A wayfinding system.
Amateurs. You don't search for a dog. Tomorrow, I hold auditions.
And I'll handle plan B.
What's plan B?
Baby, you're a lawyer. It's better if you don't know.

scenes.summary: Saturday morning. Robin tracks Tugboat down the stoop and straight to MacLaren's door, then writes it off as a nose wall. Ted unveils his flyer, which has no phone number.

beats.line: Hot dog bun. He came down these steps at a run and turned left.
Robin, are you sniffing the sidewalk?
I'm reading it.
Down the steps to MacLaren's. And then nothing.
Beer, sausage and Barney's cologne. It's a nose wall. Nothing gets through that.
Well, he's not in there. Carl once threw me out for humming.
Anyway. Behold. A three-quarter elevation. Dogs, like buildings, have a good side.
It's gorgeous, Ted. Where's the phone number?
It would have broken the grid.

scenes.summary: Saturday night at the booth. MacLaren's is mysteriously out of sausages. Barney's casting call goes live.

beats.line: Carl! The sausage platter. The big one. I'm stress-eating for two.
Out of sausages.
How is a pub out of sausages?
Busy weekend.
National dog food commercial. Seeking scruffy brown mutt, one ear up. Open call, noon tomorrow, right outside this bar.
Why would a dog read a casting call?
He won't. Whoever found him will. And right now they're looking at him thinking, that's a star.
Barney, that's actually smart.
Please. I haven't chased anything since 2004. I hold auditions.
Carl, the second a sausage comes through that door, I want—
It won't.

scenes.label: 9:00 PM
scenes.summary: Arthur calls from 'Cleveland' to sing Tugboat to sleep. Marshall hands the phone to Barney, who gets sung to.

beats.line: Nine o'clock. It's him. He's calling to say goodnight.
To you?
To the dog.
Eriksen. Status report.
Great, sir! He ate at six. One sausage. He says it was zero.
He's lying. Hold the phone to his ear. He doesn't sleep without his song.
Give it to Barney. He's the closest thing we've got.
Little tugboat, little tugboat, the harbor's dark and wide.
Close your eyes now, little tugboat. I'm right there at your side.
Is he whimpering? He does that. Goodnight, sailor.
Nobody's ever sung me to sleep.
Sung me awake, sure. Different thing.
We are finding this dog.
Sir, please don't lean on the serif.
Tugboat!
Raccoon. Old. Recently divorced.
Next. No. Next. Ma'am, that is a cat.

scenes.summary: Sunday afternoon. Lily stops a dog walker mid-walk to rent a lookalike. Mona offers a real clue about runaway dogs; Lily only wants the dog.

beats.line: Excuse me. The brown one. Third from the left.
That's Biscuit. His mom's in Aruba. I don't know her name. She's Biscuit's mom.
I'm Lily. Tugboat's aunt. He ran away Friday.
Tugboat? One ear up, sausage problem? His dad made my doorman cry.
But Tugboat doesn't run away. Dogs like him run back. Somewhere they used to need.
Love that. How much for Biscuit until nine?
He's not for rent! You can't just swap a dog!
I teach kindergarten. Our class hamster has died four times.
The kids think he's very resilient.
No.
You're walking eleven dogs. Your license says six. I took pictures.
Back by nine. And he gets the good kibble.

scenes.label: 6:45 PM
scenes.summary: Sunday evening. Every method has failed. Lily unveils plan B, Marshall refuses it, and Arthur arrives two hours early.

beats.line: Two hundred and twelve dogs. Zero Tugboats. Three phone numbers.
And I'm godfather to a Pomeranian named Steve.
My flyer got one call. A man wanted to know who did the lettering.
We're getting lunch.
My trail still ends at MacLaren's. I checked six times. Carl made me buy a drink every time.
That's it. I'm the sneeze guy now.
Plan B is in our bedroom.
Lily, what did you do?
His name is Biscuit. He's brown, one ear up, and until nine o'clock, he answers to Tugboat.
Lily, that's somebody else's dog.
For three hours. It's a timeshare.
Lilypad, I can't hand that man a fake dog.
Eriksen. Cleveland ended early.

scenes.summary: Arthur comes in. Marshall won't bring out the fake and confesses. Arthur confesses back: there was no Cleveland. Barney was the dog. Mona's clue and the building's address tell Arthur exactly where Tugboat went.

beats.line: Eriksen. Where's my boy?
Asleep, sir! Very asleep.
Biscuit. Now.
Mr. Hobbs, I lost him.
Friday night, on the roof. He slipped his collar and took my hot dog.
I've lied to you for two days. I'm not bringing a stranger's dog out of that bedroom.
There's a stranger's dog in your bedroom?
He's a temp.
There's no deposition. I spent the weekend at my office. Twelve blocks from here.
The vet says his heart is getting too big. He has a year. Maybe two.
I wanted to see if I could do a weekend.
I couldn't.
Neither could he.
For what it's worth, sir, he loved the song.
Who are you?
I was the dog.
The dog walker said he didn't run away. He ran back. Somewhere he used to need.
Eriksen. What's downstairs from this building?
A bar. MacLaren's.
Stool three.

scenes.summary: Arthur and Carl know each other. Tugboat has been asleep on Carl's feet since Friday. The trail went into the bar, the sausages went into the dog, and Arthur thanks Marshall by name.

beats.line: Carl.
Arthur.
He's back here. Been asleep on my feet since Friday.
Since Friday? Carl, we sat in that booth for six hours last night!
Nobody asked.
The trail went into the bar, Ted.
I always come back riding the moose, Ted.
Wait. How do you two know each other?
Nine years ago my wife left. I sat on this stool every night for a month. Puppy in my coat.
Carl was the only bartender in the city who'd let him in.
Him, I didn't mind.
So that's where all the sausages went.
He says he's only had one.
Marshall.
Sir?
Thank you for telling me.
Two scotches, Carl. And one sausage.
He's had fourteen.
Make it two.
Tugboat didn't have a year. He had five, and he spent most Friday nights of them under stool three.
That spring, Arthur wrote Marshall's review there. Under weaknesses, it said: lost my dog.
Under strengths: told me.
